title: Autonomic Cost Surgeon: Safe apply/rollback for batching & cache config changes
creator: Aisha Patel
description:
Background: Recent infra experiments and a production incident showed that heuristic-driven batching/cache config changes can produce cost regressions and transient SLO violations when traffic distributions shift. We need an automated subsystem that can safely apply recommended batching and KV-cache changes, detect harmful side effects quickly, and perform targeted, auditable rollbacks with state reconciliation when necessary.

Goal: Build an end-to-end 'Autonomic Cost Surgeon' that: (1) ingests batching/caching recommendations from Optimize, (2) runs a dry-run/simulation and traffic shadowing stage, (3) applies changes via staged canary rollout with economic and SLO guardrails, (4) monitors defined safety signals and triggers automated rollback when thresholds are exceeded, and (5) reconciles desired vs actual runtime state and provides human-readable remediation suggestions.

Success metrics: 1) Reduce manual rollback incidents for cost tuning by 80% in Q2; 2) Maintain 99.9% of baseline P95 latency during automated applies (within allowed hysteresis); 3) Demonstrate cost-per-token improvements for valid recommendations while keeping false-positive economic regressions below 5% of attempts.

Scope: Recommend/apply/roll back for the following config classes: batching window/size, batching timeout, KV prefix cache TTL, KV eviction thresholds, batch-splitting thresholds, and quantization profile toggles (safe subset). Exclude core kernel-level changes and model weights.

Non-goals: Rewriting routing policies, autoscaler rearchitect, or replacing human approvals for enterprise-critical customers (those remain manual unless opted-in).

Acceptance criteria: see acceptance_criteria field.

Implementation plan (high level):
1) Analyzer: extend Optimize to annotate each recommendation with an economic delta estimate and sensitivity band (expected token-level cost savings, variance under traffic shift).
2) Simulator & Shadow: a lightweight runtime simulator that replays recent token traces to estimate latency/cost under proposed config; a traffic shadowing hook to mirror a configurable ~1-2% of live requests into a canary pool without affecting downstream metrics.
3) Staged Orchestrator: apply via staged canary percentages (0.5% -> 2% -> 10% -> 50% -> full) with configurable soak windows and circuit-breakers. Each step is gated by both cost and SLO heuristics.
4) Sentinel (safety runner): real-time monitor that computes composite safety score from signals (P95 latency delta, error-rate delta, queue depth, token-cost-per-second, request tail latency) and kicks off rollback when score exceeds threshold or when an absolute guardrail is violated.
5) Reconciler & Checkpointing: persistent pre-change checkpoint of runtime config + ephemeral KV cache snapshot metadata; reconciliation loop to detect divergence (manual changes, partial apply failures) and either repair or propose automated corrective actions.
6) Observability & Runbooks: dashboards per-apply showing economic delta and safety timeline, and an auto-generated runbook entry for each automated rollback with forensic artifacts.

Rollout plan: start with internal dev clusters -> selected non-critical customer tenants (opt-in) -> wider beta on Dedicated pools -> default opt-out for hosted customers. Feature gated behind a new runtime flag and console toggle.

Risks & mitigations:
- False-positive rollbacks causing thrashing: add hysteresis, minimum time-in-state and exponential backoff between retries.
- Simulation mismatch to live traffic: shadowing stage required; conservative thresholds for first two ramp steps.
- Partial apply leaving inconsistent state: apply idempotent ops with checkpoints and a reconciliation job that can rollback partial updates or re-apply missing steps.

Docs & artifacts: PRD: https://confluence.redwood.com/display/OPS/Autonomic+Cost+Surgeon+PRD; Design notes: https://drive.redwood.com/drive/folders/1a2b3c+/cost-surgeon-design; Grafana: https://grafana.redwood.com/d/abc123/batching-latency?from=now-7d; prototype PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/runtimes/pull/3891
acceptance_criteria: System can perform a dry-run simulation and report expected cost/delta within +/-15% of observed shadow results
Staged apply flow supports 5 rollout steps with configurable soak windows and halts automatically when guardrail breached
Automated rollback executes within 90s of a critical guardrail breach and restores pre-change checkpoint state
Reconciler detects out-of-band config drift and either auto-heals to last known-good or flags human review with remediation steps
Dashboards show an economic delta and safety timeline for every apply; every automated rollback creates an auditable runbook entry
implementation_steps: Design analyzer extension and API contract between Optimize and Orchestrator
Build simulator + traffic shadowing endpoint (1-2% sampling) and validation harness
Implement staged orchestrator with configurable gates and checkpointing
Create sentinel scoring engine and define default guardrails/thresholds
Add reconciler that snapshots config and cache metadata before change and reconciles post-change
Wire observability: per-apply Grafana panels, logs, and auto-generated runbook template
Run chaos tests and cost regressions against staging traffic; iterate thresholds
Gradual rollout to dev -> beta customers -> production with opt-in controls
